Priya: hey team — priya here, first day on runtime. following the dev README and trying to build from source on Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 11.8, gcc 12. hitting an abrupt ptxas error during link. any quick pointers?
Priya: error snippet copied: 
```
ptxas fatal : ValueError: unsupported PTX version '8.7'
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudart_static
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Priya: building inside VSCode devcontainer (using nvidia runtime) with `make -j4 BUILD_USE_CUDA=1`
Mika: welcome! two things: 1) PTX version typically means driver < toolkit; 2) missing -lcudart_static suggests linker can't find static cudart (packaging variation).
Mika: what does `nvidia-smi` show? and `ptxas --version` inside the container?
Priya: inside container `nvidia-smi` -> Driver Version: 520.61.05, CUDA Version: 11.8; `ptxas --version` -> 10.6.0 (from /usr/local/cuda-11.8/bin)
Natanael: driver 520.x is likely the issue for the PTX. corp laptops often block driver updates. For the cudart_static issue, we usually either add `-L/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/stubs` or use dynamic linking.
Evan: since you're in a devcontainer, double-check the container image's CUDA toolkit vs host driver policy. If the container toolkit emits newer PTX than the host driver accepts, you'll see that PTX error. Two quick workarounds: (A) set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to only the SMs your GPU supports; (B) build with `--cudart=shared` to avoid requiring static cudart.
Priya: i'm on a T4 on laptop dock (org-managed). what's the env to force shared cudart?
Natanael: set `CUDNN_CUDA_RUNTIME=shared` or add `BUILD_CUDA_CUDART=shared` depending on the Makefile. If not present, edit linker flags: replace `-lcudart_static -ldl -lrt -pthread` with `-lcudart -ldl -lrt -pthread` in the build config.
Priya: tried changing to `-lcudart`, now the link proceeds further but ptxas still complains.
Mika: try narrowing generated PTX: before build `export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5;7.0;6.1"` (match your GPU). That prevents nvcc from emitting PTX v8.7. Also run `nvcc --list-gpus` to confirm compute capability.
Priya: `nvidia-smi` says GPU: T4, cc 7.5. set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to 7.5, rebuild — it moves past ptxas now but fails at runtime with missing symbol `cublasLtCreate` when I run unit tests in container
Evan: runtime missing symbol = host driver doesn't expose newer cublas symbols. Two options: (1) run tests on infra GPU runners (drivers 525+) or (2) test non-GPU parts locally and rely on CI for GPU tests.
Priya: infra-bot mentioned a dev image in onboarding docs earlier, is there a tagged image I should use for reproducible builds?
infra-bot: Recommended devcontainer image: registry.redwood/internal/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-gcc12-devcontainer-2026-03-01. CI runners use driver >= 525.85.
Mika: if you can't get driver bump on laptop, use the devcontainer for builds but be aware container GPU passthrough still depends on host driver for runtime. For pure build artifacts (binaries) that don't run GPU code you can use the container; for end-to-end tests use infra GPU runners.
Priya: ok that clarifies. one other sticky point: inside container `ldd` on the built binary lists `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11 => not found` even though the file exists. any trick?
Natanael: that happens if the runtime linker search path is different in container. Try `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before running or add `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64` to LDFLAGS during link so the binary embeds the path.
Priya: adding rpath fixed the runtime missing libs inside container. after that, unit tests that don't call cublas pass locally. GPU-heavy tests still fail (expected).
Evan: sounds like you're in the expected state for a corp-managed laptop. For onboarding checklist, we normally document: driver min versions (525+ for CUDA 11.8), TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST fallback, how to switch to shared cudart, rpath/LD_LIBRARY_PATH tip, and use infra dev image + CI GPU runners for validation.
Priya: i'll draft a short onboarding note with commands I used (nvcc/nvidia-smi checks, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST example, LDFLAGS rpath tweak, and link-order note). will drop it in eng-runtime docs and ping @Mika to review.
Mika: please do, and welcome to the team! happy to pair on first-week task if you want. :wave:
Priya: thanks everyone 44b — saved me a ton of time. will post the doc and a tiny gist of the exact env vars/Makefile diffs shortly.
